payload.title: fix(data-warehouse): split oversized batches to avoid delta offset overflow

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview Fixes recurring delta-rs "Offset overflow error" on incremental warehouse syncs caused by Arrow `string`/`binary`/`list` columns crossing the 32-bit offset limit (2³¹). The `Batcher` previously bypassed its byte cap for `pa.Table` inputs, letting wide SQL-source tables reach delta-rs at sizes that overflowed during merge. The fix measures true 32-bit-offset pressure per column, recursively row-halves any oversized table into zero-copy slices below ~1.4 GiB, and adapts both V2 and V3 pipeline loops to drain the resulting queue of tables. **Changes:** - Added `_column_offset_pressure` / `_max_offset_pressure` / `_split_to_offset_limit` helpers and a new `DEFAULT_MAX_COLUMN_OFFSET_BYTES = 1.5 GB` knob to `Batcher`; `Batcher` now holds a queue (`_ready`) and splits incoming tables on `batch()`. - Updated V2 and V3 pipeline run loops to drain ready chunks with `while batcher.should_yield()` (both during iteration and final flush) and made V3 also increment `chunk_index` in the flush path. - Added unit-test coverage for the new helpers and Batcher splitting behavior, including type-specific offset pressure, order/data preservation, single-row termination, no-op under limit, and the buffered-list path. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline/batcher.py | Introduces offset-pressure measurement and recursive row-halving; converts `Batcher` from single-ready-table to ready-table queue with new `max_column_offset_bytes` parameter. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline/pipeline.py | V2 run loop drains all ready chunks via `while`; flush loop also iterates and now increments `chunk_index`. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline_v3/pipeline.py | V3 run/flush loops mirror V2 to consume the queue, ensuring metrics and `chunk_index` are updated per emitted chunk. | | posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline/test/test_batcher.py | Adds parameterized helper tests and Batcher-level tests for splitting, no-op under limit, single-row termination, and buffered-list splitting. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline/batcher.py:131-139
**Silent buffer discard for `pa.Table` items when dict data is buffered**

The unconditional `self._buffer = []; self._buffer_size_bytes = 0` at lines 138–139 runs for all three branches that reach `_set_ready`, including `isinstance(item, pa.Table)`. If a caller has accumulated dict rows in `_buffer` (below the flush threshold) and then calls `batch(pa_table)`, those buffered rows are silently dropped. The same behaviour existed in the original code (the `_py_table` path in the old `get_table()` also cleared `_buffer`), so this is not a new regression, and in practice SQL sources only ever emit `pa.Table` items while dict-based sources only ever emit dicts. Still, a defensive guard — or at least matching the comment to the actual branch — would make the invariant explicit to future callers.

### Issue 2 of 2
posthog/temporal/data_imports/pipelines/pipeline/batcher.py:155
**`list.pop(0)` is O(n)**

`self._ready.pop(0)` shifts every remaining element left on each call. In the overflow path `_ready` holds O(log N) elements, so this is negligible in practice, but using `collections.deque` with `popleft()` — or reversing the list and calling `pop()` — would make this O(1) at no other cost.


`````

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview Restores the use of `psycopg.Cursor(connection)` directly when applying the session-level `SET statement_timeout` on the Postgres streaming connection. Because the connection is opened with `cursor_factory=psycopg.ServerCursor` for non-read-replica syncs, the previous `connection.cursor()` call raised a `ServerCursor.__init__() missing 'name'` error that was silently swallowed at DEBUG, leaving the 10-minute timeout unset. **Changes:** - Replace `connection.cursor()` with `psycopg.Cursor(connection)` to bypass the ServerCursor factory when setting `statement_timeout`. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

`````markdown
---

### Issue 1 of 1
posthog/temporal/data_modeling/activities/materialize_view.py:579-588
**Drain loop not cancellation-safe under activity cancellation**

If Temporal cancels the activity while the drain loop is sleeping, `await asyncio.sleep(0.05)` raises `CancelledError`, which propagates immediately out of the `finally` block — `await producer_task` is never reached. If the producer is simultaneously blocked on `await asyncio.to_thread(batch_queue.put, SENTINEL)` (queue still full because nothing drained it), the thread pool thread holding that `put` is orphaned until the GC eventually drops the queue, and the producer task itself is left un-awaited. Wrapping the drain section in `try/except asyncio.CancelledError` (re-raising after awaiting the task) or guarding with `asyncio.shield(producer_task)` would close this gap.


`````

<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
products/user_interviews/frontend/TranscriptChat.tsx:19
The `g` flag on `TURN_SPLIT_RE` is superfluous: `String.prototype.split()` does not use `lastIndex` and ignores `g` (it resets the index internally per the spec). Leaving `g` on a module-level regex constant adds noise and is a trap for any future caller that uses `exec()` or `test()` on the same constant, since those methods will resume from `lastIndex` and produce wrong results on the second call.

```suggestion
const TURN_SPLIT_RE = /\b(AI|Assistant|Interviewer|User|Interviewee):\s+/
```

### Issue 2 of 2
products/user_interviews/frontend/TranscriptChat.test.tsx:34-41
**Speaker label inside content causes incorrect split**

The `'colons in user content do not split'` test only guards against bare colons; it doesn't protect against a recognised speaker word appearing inside spoken text (e.g. `'AI: I asked the User: about it. User: Sure.'`). Because `TURN_SPLIT_RE` uses `\b` rather than anchoring to line-start or sentence-start, "User:" mid-sentence matches exactly like a turn delimiter, splitting the AI's reply and creating a spurious turn. Adding a parameterised case for this scenario would document the limitation and catch any future regex change that makes it worse.


`````

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 Automated comment by **QA Swarm** — not written by a human
>
> Multi-perspective review: qa-team (specialists + generalists), paul-reviewer, xp-reviewer, security-audit

## Verdict: ⚠️ REQUEST CHANGES

The chat-bubble component, tests, and stories are well shaped — pure parser separated from rendering, parameterized tests, the Storybook coverage really helps. The main risk is in `parseTranscript`: three independent reviewers (qa-team, paul, xp) all landed on the same concern that the word-boundary regex will mis-attribute or scramble bubbles the moment a transcript contains a speaker keyword inside a turn body.

### Key findings

- 🟠 **HIGH (convergent x3)** — `parseTranscript` regex matches speaker tokens anywhere, not just at line starts; also case-sensitive while the classifier is case-insensitive (`TranscriptChat.tsx:19`).
- 🟡 **MEDIUM (convergent x2)** — Leading prose before the first speaker prefix is silently discarded (`TranscriptChat.tsx:34`).
- 🟡 **MEDIUM** — No observability on the fallback path; can't tell from production what % of transcripts hit it (`TranscriptChat.tsx:59`).
- 🟢 **LOW (convergent x3)** — `ProfilePicture` is fed a full display name as `first_name`, and non-email identifiers (raw distinct_ids) are surfaced verbatim in the chat UI (`TranscriptChat.tsx:113`).
- 🟢 **LOW** — Display-name fallback chain is duplicated in three places (`TranscriptChat.tsx:124`).
- 🟢 **LOW** — AI bubble background matches page surface — looks like a floating border (`TranscriptChat.tsx:88`).
- 🟢 **LOW (convergent x2)** — Missing parameterized tests for the two real-world failure modes (mid-sentence keyword, leading prose).

### Convergence

The strongest signal is the line-anchoring concern at `TranscriptChat.tsx:19` — flagged independently by three reviewers (qa-team/data-integrity, paul, xp). Convergent findings carry the highest confidence.

### Reviewer summaries

| Reviewer | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| 🔍 qa-team | Component is safe (LemonMarkdown is `skipHtml`); parser's mid-sentence false splits and leading-prose drop are the substantive concerns. |
| 👤 paul | Stamp anyway — the two things to chat about are the upstream coupling/fragility of recovering structure from free-text and the lack of observability on the fallback path. |
| 📐 xp | Small, well-shaped change in the right XP spirit; tighten the parser contract and add two more parameterized cases to lock the behaviour in. |
| 🛡 security-audit | No new vulnerabilities introduced — XSS surface unchanged from baseline, MD5 Gravatar URL safe, no new endpoints or trust boundaries. |

---

`````markdown
### Issue 1 of 1
nodejs/src/logs-ingestion/logs-ingestion-consumer.test.ts:1155-1183
The new test only exercises the 90d tier and negatively asserts 30d/14d are absent, but it never runs the same scenario for 14d or 30d. Since there are exactly three tiers, a parameterised test would cover all cases without duplicated setup — and the project rule explicitly prefers parameterised tests.

```suggestion
        it.each([
            { retentionDays: 14, absent: ['bytes_ingested_retention_30d', 'bytes_ingested_retention_90d'] },
            { retentionDays: 30, absent: ['bytes_ingested_retention_14d', 'bytes_ingested_retention_90d'] },
            { retentionDays: 90, absent: ['bytes_ingested_retention_14d', 'bytes_ingested_retention_30d'] },
        ])(
            'should emit only bytes_ingested_retention_${retentionDays}d for the matching tier',
            async ({ retentionDays, absent }) => {
                const usageStats = new Map([
                    [
                        team.id,
                        {
                            bytesReceived: 500,
                            recordsReceived: 5,
                            bytesAllowed: 500,
                            recordsAllowed: 5,
                            bytesDropped: 0,
                            recordsDropped: 0,
                            piiReplacements: 0,
                            retentionDays,
                        },
                    ],
                ])

                await consumer['emitUsageMetrics'](usageStats)

                const messages = getProducedKafkaMessages().filter((m) => m.topic === KAFKA_APP_METRICS_2)
                const retentionMetric = messages
                    .map((m) => parseMetricValue(m.value))
                    .find((m) => m?.metric_name === `bytes_ingested_retention_${retentionDays}d`)

                expect(retentionMetric?.count).toBe(500)
                const metricNames = messages.map((m) => parseMetricValue(m.value)?.metric_name)
                for (const name of absent) {
                    expect(metricNames).not.toContain(name)
                }
            }
        )
```
`````

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
frontend/src/layout/scenes/ConfigurePromotedProductModal.tsx:29-33
**Stale modal state on every open**

`ConfigurePromotedProductModal` is always mounted in `GlobalModals`, so these `useState` initializers run once — during the very first render — at which point `promotedProductLogic.afterMount` hasn't fired yet and `effectiveTarget` is `null`. As a result, `pendingKind` is always `'product'` and `pendingProduct` is always `'product_analytics'` regardless of the user's actual intent. A user whose team picked `session_replay` during onboarding will see "Product analytics" pre-selected every time they open this modal.

The same problem causes the state to go stale after "Reset to onboarding default": `clearOverride` removes the override and closes the modal, but when the modal is reopened the picker still shows whatever kind/value was active in the previous interaction, not the reverted effectiveTarget.

Fix: add a `useEffect` that resets the three pieces of pending state from `effectiveTarget` whenever `isOpen` transitions to `true`.

### Issue 2 of 2
frontend/src/layout/scenes/ConfigurePromotedProductModal.tsx:20-23
**Inconsistent product labels between modal and nav item (DRY / OnceAndOnlyOnce)**

The modal builds labels inline with `key.replace(/_/g, ' ').replace(/^(.)/, (c) => c.toUpperCase())`, which only uppercases the very first character. For `llm_analytics` this yields `"Llm analytics"`, while `PRODUCT_KEY_LABELS` in `PromotedProductNavItem.tsx` correctly maps the same key to `"LLM analytics"`. Exporting and reusing `PRODUCT_KEY_LABELS` from the nav-item file (or a shared location) would keep both in sync and express the mapping exactly once.

```suggestion
// Import PRODUCT_KEY_LABELS from PromotedProductNavItem (or a shared constants file)
// to keep nav-item labels and modal labels in sync (currently `llm_analytics` renders
// as "Llm analytics" here vs "LLM analytics" in the nav item).
const PRODUCT_OPTIONS = Object.keys(PRODUCT_KEY_TO_URL).map((key) => ({
    value: key,
    label: PRODUCT_KEY_LABELS[key] ?? key.replace(/_/g, ' ').replace(/^(.)/, (c) => c.toUpperCase()),
}))
```


`````

</details>

## Verdict: ⚠️ REQUEST CHANGES

Solid foundation — flag-gated, 4-arm A/B+A/A, real consumer, good observability (3 distinct events), parameterized variant-gating test. But the cold-cache + Redis-degraded paths in the server-side template render are a real risk for the 75% control population, and a few simplifications would be cheap to land before this graduates beyond the experiment.

### Key findings

**HIGH**
- 🔴 `posthog/utils.py:588` — ClickHouse query on hot template-render path runs for all users (incl. control). Gate behind the flag + wrap in try/except. **Convergent (paul + qa-team/reliability)**

**MEDIUM**
- `promoted_product_lookup.py:16` — query has no `timestamp >=` bound; full team-partition scan for teams with no intent events. **Convergent (paul + qa-team/database)**
- `ConfigurePromotedProductModal.tsx:20` — `PRODUCT_OPTIONS` regex produces "Llm analytics" / "Ai chat" (wrong casing per CLAUDE.md), and is the 3rd parallel map over the same key domain. Extract one shared record. **Convergent (paul + xp)**
- `productSelectionLogic.ts:300` — onboarding writes to a localStorage key from another feature with no shared constant import (paul)
- `NavLink.tsx:44` — `sideAction` prop has one consumer; Home's cog is still a hard-coded special case sitting next to it (xp)
- `promotedProductLogic.ts:73` — variant string re-checked at 4+ sites; extract `variantShowsEntry` / `variantAllowsOverride` predicates (xp)
- `api/team.py:2015` — endpoint has no frontend consumer (MCP-only). Worth documenting in PR description (xp)

**Positive findings worth noting (no action needed)**
- ✅ Tenant isolation is correct — `self.get_object()` enforces, `team_id` filter in ClickHouse query, parameterized, `LIMIT 1`
- ✅ ProductKey enum whitelist in `_fetch_from_clickhouse` neutralizes any XSS-via-hostile-event vector into APP_CONTEXT
- ✅ Redis cache key is tenant-scoped
- ✅ MCP variant gate is for experiment scoping, not isolation — isolation already enforced at API layer

### Convergence

Three convergent findings — each flagged independently by ≥2 reviewers (highest confidence):
- Template-render-time ClickHouse on hot path (paul + qa-team)
- Missing timestamp bound on ClickHouse query (paul + qa-team)
- Triple-map duplication + wrong-casing modal (paul + xp)

### Reviewer summaries

| Reviewer | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| 👤 paul | "nice shape… my main worry is the localStorage cross-feature coupling… second worry is the template-render-time clickhouse call… none of it is blocking — i'd ship this as an experiment and tighten on the way" |
| 📐 xp | "make-it-work is done; the make-it-right pass should unify the product-key registry, name the variant predicates, and decide whether the API endpoint is load-bearing or YAGNI" |
| 🛡 qa-team (security/db/reliability) | "PR is tenant-safe. The main reliability concerns are: (1) the ClickHouse query has no timestamp bound and could scan deeply on cold-cache, (2) a degraded Redis would cause the server-render path to retry ClickHouse on every request. Neither is blocking; both are worth tracking. No tenant-isolation or data-integrity defects." |

payload.author: greptile-apps
payload.body:
<!-- greptile_other_comments_section -->

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
tools/phrocs/internal/process/proc_test.go:283-301
**Batching behavior is no longer asserted despite the test name**

The test is named `TestReadLoop_batchesOutput` but the rewrite drops both `OutputMsg` count checks entirely. `runReadLoop` creates an internal `outChannel` and discards every message that lands in it — the caller has no way to count `OutputMsg` values after the call returns. If the `readLoop` flush interval or coalescing logic regresses and starts emitting one message per line instead of a handful, this test passes anyway. Consider either renaming the test to reflect its new, weaker scope, or extending `runReadLoop` (e.g. return the drained `[]tea.Msg` slice) so the batching assertion can be expressed cleanly on top of the deterministic reader.

### Issue 2 of 2
tools/phrocs/internal/process/proc_test.go:297-300
The `totalLines/2` floor (250 out of 500) was chosen to tolerate PTY data loss, but with a deterministic `strings.NewReader` there is no race and all 500 lines should always be present. The permissive threshold means the test would pass even if `readLoop` silently discarded half the input. Tighten it to catch real regressions.

```suggestion
	lines := p.Lines()
	if len(lines) < totalLines {
		t.Fatalf("expected all %d buffered lines, got %d", totalLines, len(lines))
	}
```


`````

</details>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
posthog/session_recordings/session_recording_api.py:2126-2127
Unbounded `any-user` exclusion set — for a large, active team the `DISTINCT` query could return tens of thousands of session IDs, producing an oversized `NOT IN (...)` literal in ClickHouse and a correspondingly slow or oversized query. Adding a reasonable cap (e.g. the same `RECORDINGS_LIMIT` used elsewhere, or a date-bounded window) would protect against this. The `current-user` branch is naturally bounded by one user's history, but the team-wide branch has no guard.

```suggestion
    if hide_viewed_recordings == HideViewedRecordings.ANY_USER:
        return list(
            SessionRecordingViewed.objects.filter(team=team)
            .values_list("session_id", flat=True)
            .distinct()
            .order_by("-id")[:10_000]
        )
```

### Issue 2 of 2
posthog/session_recordings/session_recording_api.py:1996
**`not query_for_list.session_ids` treats an empty list the same as `None`** — the comment says "skip when explicit session_ids are requested", but `not []` is truthy, so `session_ids_to_exclude` is computed even when `session_ids` is an explicit empty list (e.g. when all requested recordings were found in Postgres and `remaining_session_ids` resolves to `[]`). In practice this is harmless because `session_id IN []` returns no rows anyway, but `if query_for_list.session_ids is None:` would more precisely match the stated intent and be consistent with the `isinstance` check in the query builder.


`````

</details>

`````markdown
posthog/admin/test_admin.py:178-182
The team prefers parameterised tests. A `for` loop over models in a single test method means a failure on the first unregistered model silences all subsequent ones. `@pytest.mark.parametrize` gives independent pass/fail signals per model and clearer CI output.

```suggestion
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "model",
        [HogFlow, HogFlowTemplate, HogFlowBatchJob, HogFunction, Plugin, PluginConfig],
        ids=lambda m: m.__name__,
    )
    def test_moved_product_models_are_registered(self, model):
        # Tests skip the lazy admin registry, so trigger registration explicitly.
        register_all_admin()
        assert admin.site.is_registered(model), f"{model.__name__} is not registered in Django admin"
```
`````

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
.github/scripts/assign-reviewers.test.js:46-54
**Non-parameterized test for `classifyOwner`**

The team convention is to prefer parameterized tests. This single test body checks three independent `(input, expected)` pairs (team, user, malformed), but it uses a plain `test()` rather than `test.each()`. If one assertion fails, Jest still runs the others in the same block, making it harder to tell exactly which case broke. Each case should be its own `test.each` row so failures are isolated and labelled.

### Issue 2 of 2
.github/scripts/assign-reviewers.test.js:158-167
**`never caps explicit users` test doesn't exercise the cap bypass**

All users in this test have `lines: 50`, which clears `substantiveLines: 10`, so every user lands in `requested` before the team-cap logic even runs — the cap is never evaluated for users. The test would pass identically if users were subject to the same cap as teams. A test that truly verifies the bypass should mix overflowing teams with users (e.g. 6 teams + 2 users, all substantive) and assert that all users survive while the smallest teams are demoted.


`````

### Key Takeaways

1. **Wall clock is 37s better in this PR** despite using fewer shards — the tighter spread pays off more than extra parallelism with imbalanced distribution.

2. **Auto-size has better averages/P50** (more shards → lower per-shard load), but this is negated by much worse tail latency (max). Spread is 197–252s worse across the main segments.

If a regression silently changes which predicate is broken, the test output won't identify which case failed. Splitting these into individual `@parameterized.expand` cases — one for the included case and one each for each exclusion reason — gives a failing test name that immediately names the broken contract.

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 1
posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/common/registry.py:15-25
`_loaded` is set to `True` before `load_all_sources()` finishes. If any source module raises an `ImportError` partway through `_load_all.py` (e.g., a broken optional dependency), the exception propagates to the first caller, but `_loaded` is already `True`. Every subsequent call to `_ensure_loaded` returns immediately, leaving the registry permanently incomplete for the lifetime of the process — subsequent lookups either silently return a partial source list or raise a `ValueError` for the missing source, with no indication that loading ever failed.

```suggestion
    @classmethod
    def _ensure_loaded(cls) -> None:
        # Sources self-register via @SourceRegistry.register on import. We import them
        # on first registry use rather than at package import, so a process that never
        # touches the registry (most of them) doesn't pay for every vendor SDK at startup.
        if cls._loaded:
            return
        cls._loaded = True
        try:
            from posthog.temporal.data_imports.sources import load_all_sources

            load_all_sources()
        except Exception:
            cls._loaded = False
            raise
```


`````

</details>

<details><summary>Prompt To Fix All With AI</summary>

`````markdown
Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes.

---

### Issue 1 of 2
posthog/hogql/test/test_query.py:2042-2051
The test only exercises the `ExposedHogQLError` branch of the error-preservation logic. When `prepare_ast_for_printing` raises a generic (non-`ExposedHogQLError`) exception the error message falls back to `"Unknown error"` — that branch is untested. Per the team's preference for parameterised tests, both cases would fit neatly here.

```suggestion
    @parameterized.expand(
        [
            ("exposed_hogql_error", ExposedHogQLError("debug failure"), "debug failure"),
            ("generic_exception", Exception("unexpected"), "Unknown error"),
        ]
    )
    @patch("posthog.hogql.query.sync_execute")
    def test_debug_mode_preserves_prepare_error_without_executing_clickhouse(
        self, _name, exc, expected_error, mock_sync_execute
    ):
        with patch("posthog.hogql.query.prepare_ast_for_printing", side_effect=exc):
            response = execute_hogql_query("SELECT 1", team=self.team, modifiers=HogQLQueryModifiers(debug=True))

        self.assertEqual(response.error, expected_error)
        self.assertEqual(response.clickhouse, "")
        mock_sync_execute.assert_not_called()
```

### Issue 2 of 2
posthog/hogql/query.py:888-892
The string `"Unknown error"` is now used in two separate places: inside `_generate_clickhouse_sql` (line 718) and here in `execute()`. Extracting it to a module-level constant would keep it OnceAndOnlyOnce and make any future change automatically consistent.

```suggestion
                    if self.clickhouse_sql == "":
                        if self.error is None:
                            self.error = _UNKNOWN_QUERY_ERROR
                    else:
                        self._execute_clickhouse_query()
```
`````
